3. Test RepeatMasker recovery rate (5 replicates per scenario)

Heatmap cells show the mean of the replicate recovery rates; a replicate with no simulated TE in a cell is skipped, and cells empty in all 5 replicates are grey. Numbers in the cells are the mean number of simulated TEs per replicate (k = thousands). Marginal bars show the pooled rate of each slice, sum(recovered) / sum(total), computed within each replicate and then summarised as mean ± SD across the 5 replicates.

3.4 Binomial GLMM: identity vs integrity dependence

Recovery rises steeply with identity (≈0 below 0.5, ≈0.95 above 0.75), while integrity only matters in the lowest bin (< 0.1), where recovery plateaus at ≈0.70-0.77 even at identity 0.95. The main model is built to follow that shape, per scenario:

cbind(recovered, total - recovered) ~ ns(identity, df = 3) * integrity_low + (1 | rep) + (1 | obs)

  • ns(identity, df = 3): natural cubic spline of the identity bin midpoint (allows the threshold). df is capped at (number of identity bins - 2) so the spline cannot pass through every point and oscillate between them; scenario 4 has only 4 identity bins and gets df = 2.
  • integrity_low: integrity bin [0.0-0.1) vs the rest (>=0.1, the reference level).
  • (1 | obs): observation-level random effect per cell × replicate, absorbing the extra-binomial variation between cells (the dispersion ratio, Pearson χ² / residual df, should be ≤ 1).
  • rep_sd near 0 (singular fit) means the replicates do not differ beyond sampling noise.

Likelihood-ratio tests (LRT) drop all terms involving one variable (main effect + interaction). With ~180,000 TEs per replicate almost any term is significant, so compare the size of the LRT statistics rather than p-values. The two linear models (identity and integrity as bin midpoints, centred at 0.5 and scaled so one unit is one bin; odds ratios per 0.1 increase) are kept for reference: they cannot follow the identity threshold or the low-integrity plateau, so their integrity statistics understate the effect of the lowest integrity bin.

A: LRT χ² of the main model for dropping the identity terms vs the integrity terms. B: recovery rate against identity. Large points with error bars are pooled rates, sum(recovered) / sum(total), for integrity < 0.1 and ≥ 0.1 (mean ± SD of the 5 replicates); small light points are the 9 individual integrity bins ≥ 0.1 (mean of replicate rates), showing that they behave alike. Lines are the main GLMM’s fixed-effect predictions (random effects at 0, i.e. a typical cell).
